# Create New Project
<!-- DO NOT EDIT this file directly. It is maintained by fhc sync and will be overwritten.
     Source: templates/skills/new-project/SKILL.md in fh-commons -->

Create a new project in the fh-commons ecosystem with full scaffolding, Forgejo integration, and template sync.

## Usage

```
Run the new-project skill with <project-name> [--cli <name>] [--description "<desc>"] [--type python|webapp|ios|docs-only] [--audience internal|external] [--public] [--skip-forgejo]
Run the new-project skill                     # interactive — will gather requirements
```

**Examples:**
```
Run the new-project skill with my-app --cli ma --description "My new application"
Run the new-project skill with my-webapp --cli mw --description "My webapp" --type webapp
Run the new-project skill with my-lib --cli ml --description "Public library" --audience external
Run the new-project skill with docs-site --cli ds --description "Documentation site" --public
Run the new-project skill                     # interactive mode — asks for all details
```

**Arguments:** `$ARGUMENTS`

---

## CRITICAL: Tool Constraints

| Rule | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Use `flu`, not `gh`** | All Forgejo operations go through `flu` — GitHub CLI (`gh`) does not work with this Forgejo instance |
| **No interactive prompts** | Always provide all flags explicitly to `flu project create` — Claude Code cannot respond to interactive prompts |
| **Use `--force` and `--confirm-new-project`** | The slash command does its own confirmation, so pass `--force` to skip the CLI's built-in prompts; also pass `--confirm-new-project` which is the required safety gate for creating new projects |
| **No autonomous creation** | The new-project skill requires human approval — if running in a pipeline or autonomous mode, abort immediately with a clear message |
| **Never modify global settings** | Do NOT modify `~/.claude/settings.json` or `~/.claude/settings.local.json` — global hook installation is a separate explicit human action |

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Before starting, verify the environment is ready:

```bash
# 1. Verify Forgejo API is accessible
flu issue list > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo "API OK" || echo "API FAILED"

# 2. Verify project commands work
flu project list

# 3. Verify project name is not already taken
flu project list --all | grep -i "<project-name>"
```

- **If API fails:** Check Forgejo connectivity — `flu config show` for API URL and token status
- **If project name already exists (active):** Show error — "Project '<name>' already exists. Choose a different name."
- **If project name already exists (archived):** Suggest `flu project unarchive <name>` instead of creating new

## Argument Handling

Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for project details:

| Argument | Source | Required |
|----------|--------|----------|
| Project name | First positional argument in `$ARGUMENTS` | Yes |
| CLI command | `--cli <name>` flag, or derived from project name | No (has default) |
| Description | `--description "<text>"` flag | Yes |
| Type | `--type python\|webapp\|ios\|docs-only` flag (default: python) | No |
| Audience | `--audience internal\|external` flag (default: internal) | No |
| Visibility | `--public` or `--private` (default: private) | No |
| Skip Forgejo | `--skip-forgejo` flag | No |

**If arguments are provided:** Extract values and proceed to step 1.

**If no arguments provided (interactive mode):** Use `AskUserQuestion` to gather all requirements (see next section).

---

## Gather Requirements (Interactive Mode)

If any required detail is missing from `$ARGUMENTS`, use `AskUserQuestion` to collect:

1. **Project name** — lowercase, hyphen-separated (e.g., `my-project`)
   - Must not conflict with an existing project
   - Must not conflict with a system command

2. **Description** — one-line description of the project's purpose

3. **CLI command name** — short alias for the project CLI (default: first 3 letters of project name)
   - Verify not taken: `which <cli-name> 2>/dev/null`

4. **Project type** — python (default), webapp, ios, or docs-only

5. **Project audience** — internal (default) or external
   - External audience defaults Forgejo visibility to public

6. **Repository visibility** — private (default) or public

7. **Docker stack needed?** — yes/no
   - If yes, will offer the new-stack skill after project creation is complete

---

## Human Approval Gate

**MANDATORY: Do NOT proceed to project creation without explicit human approval.**

After gathering all arguments (from flags or interactive mode), present the following summary and ask for confirmation:

### Present Summary

Show the user exactly what will be created:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| **Project Name** | `<name>` |
| **CLI Command** | `<cli-name>` |
| **Path** | `/mnt/dev/<name>` |
| **Type** | `<type>` |
| **Forgejo Repo** | `jpierce/<name>` |
| **Visibility** | `<visibility>` |
| **Audience** | `<audience>` |
| **Description** | `<description>` |

### Require Confirmation

Use `AskUserQuestion` to ask:

> "Review the project details above. Type **yes** to create this project, or **no** to cancel."

- **If user confirms ("yes"):** Proceed to Instructions section below.
- **If user declines or gives any other answer:** Abort immediately. Do NOT create any files, repos, or config entries. Output: "Project creation cancelled."
- **If running in autonomous pipeline mode (no human present):** You MUST NOT create projects autonomously. Exit immediately with: "Project creation requires human approval. Cannot proceed in autonomous mode."

### Test/Temporary Projects

If the project name starts with `test-` or `tmp-`:
- Still require human approval — do not skip confirmation
- After creation, do NOT commit the projects.json change to main
- Inform the user: "This is a temporary project. The projects.json entry will not be committed to the main branch."

---

## Instructions

### 1. Create the Project

```bash
flu project create <name> \
  --cli <cli-name> \
  --description "<description>" \
  [--type python|webapp|ios|docs-only] \
  [--audience internal|external] \
  [--private|--public] \
  [--skip-forgejo] \
  --force \
  --confirm-new-project
```

**Expected output:** Progress messages for each scaffolding step (directory creation, git init, Forgejo repo, CLI symlink, projects.json registration).

**Error handling:**

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| "Project already exists" | Name collision | Choose a different name or run `flu project list --all` |
| "CLI name conflicts" | CLI alias taken by another project or system command | Use `--cli` flag with a different name |
| "Forgejo API error" | Token expired or server unreachable | Check `flu config show` and verify API connectivity |
| "Permission denied" | Filesystem permissions | Check write access to the project root directory |

### 2. Verify Project Creation

```bash
flu project verify <name>
```

This checks all project components:
- Directory structure exists
- Git repository initialized
- Forgejo remote configured (if not `--skip-forgejo`)
- CLI symlink installed
- projects.json entry correct

**If any checks fail:**
```bash
flu project repair <name>
```

Then re-run `flu project verify <name>` to confirm all checks pass.

### 3. Sync Templates

```bash
flu sync
```

This propagates to the new project:
- Claude slash commands (`.claude/commands/`)
- Git hooks and workflows
- Issue templates
- Root files (`CLAUDE.md`, etc.)

**Verify sync completed for the new project** — check that key files were created:
```bash
ls <project-path>/.claude/commands/ | head -5
ls <project-path>/CLAUDE.md
```

### 4. Verify CLI Works

Test the new project's CLI command:

```bash
# Basic CLI functionality
<cli-name> git status

# Forgejo integration (skip if --skip-forgejo was used)
<cli-name> issue list

# Project ecosystem visibility
<cli-name> project list
```

**If CLI command not found:**
- Check symlink exists: `ls -la ~/.local/bin/<cli-name>`
- If missing, repair: `flu project repair <name>`

**If `issue list` fails:**
- Verify Forgejo repo was created: check Forgejo web UI
- Check git remote: `git -C <project-path> remote -v`

### 5. Verify Project in Ecosystem

```bash
flu project list
```

Confirm the new project appears in the list with active status.

```bash
flu project list --verbose | grep -A 3 "<name>"
```

Verify all fields are correct: name, CLI command, path, status.

### 6. Optional: Scaffold Docker Stack

If the user indicated the project needs a Docker stack during requirements gathering:

> "Project created successfully. To set up a Docker stack, run the new-stack skill with <project-name>."

If the user did not request a Docker stack, skip this step.

**Do NOT run the new-stack skill automatically** — it is a separate workflow that requires its own user input.

### 7. Final Summary

Display the results:

```
===============================================
 Project Created: <project-name>
===============================================

  Directory:       /mnt/dev/<name>
  CLI Command:     <cli-name>
  Forgejo Repo:    jpierce/<name> (or: skipped)
  Visibility:      private/public
  Templates:       Synced
  Docker Stack:    Use the new-stack skill (or: not requested)
  Status:          Active ✓

  Quick start:
    cd /mnt/dev/<name>
    <cli-name> git status
    <cli-name> issue list

===============================================
```

## Edge Cases

| Edge Case | How to Handle |
|-----------|--------------|
| Project name conflicts with existing | Show error, suggest different name |
| Project name conflicts with archived | Suggest `flu project unarchive <name>` |
| CLI name conflicts with system command | Warn user, ask for alternative CLI name |
| CLI name conflicts with another project | Show which project owns it, ask for alternative |
| Forgejo API unreachable | Offer `--skip-forgejo` and create repo later |
| Sync fails for new project | Run `flu project repair <name>`, then re-sync |
| Project path already exists on disk | `flu project create` handles this — will error. Clean up or use `--reconfigure` |

---

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| "Project already exists" | Name collision in projects.json | `flu project list --all` to check; choose different name |
| CLI command not found after create | Symlink not installed | `flu project repair <name>` |
| Forgejo repo creation failed | API token expired or server down | `flu config show` to check; create repo manually from web UI |
| Sync did not reach new project | Project not in projects.json | `flu project verify <name>` then `flu sync` |
| `project verify` shows failures | Incomplete creation | `flu project repair <name>` |
| Git remote not configured | Forgejo repo missing or not linked | `git -C <path> remote add origin <url>` |
| Permission denied on project path | Filesystem permissions | Check ownership of parent directory |
| `--reconfigure` needed | Project dir exists but not registered | `flu project create <name> --reconfigure` |

---

## What This Command Does NOT Do

- **Does NOT set up CI/CD pipelines** — no automated build/deploy configuration
- **Does NOT create database schemas** — use the new-stack skill with database options if needed
- **Does NOT configure reverse proxy entries** — use the new-stack skill for Caddy/DNS setup
- **Does NOT start any services** — project is code-only until a Docker stack is added
- **Does NOT create initial issues or milestones** — run the research skill with <description> after project setup
- **Does NOT configure monitoring** — add to Uptime Kuma manually if needed

For Docker stacks, use the new-stack skill after project creation.

## Quick Reference

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Create project | `flu project create <name> --description "..." --cli <cli> --force --confirm-new-project` |
| Create webapp | `flu project create <name> --description "..." --type webapp --force --confirm-new-project` |
| Create external (public) | `flu project create <name> --description "..." --audience external --force --confirm-new-project` |
| Verify project | `flu project verify <name>` |
| Repair project | `flu project repair <name>` |
| Sync templates | `flu sync` |
| List projects | `flu project list` |
| List all (incl. archived) | `flu project list --all` |
| Reconfigure existing | `flu project create <name> --reconfigure` |
| Archive project | Run the archive-project skill with <name> |
